message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have phenotyping_reported aligned to abdominal aortic aneurysm (one is explicitly prevalent: PGS000753). Among them, PGS003972 comes from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023) with broad multi-cohort development (many AAA-relevant cohorts listed) and a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), which domain guidance suggests should generally outrank pan-trait/portability framework scores when endpoint fidelity is similar. Competing models include framework/portability-style scores with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS001784: PRS-CS-auto from a global-biobank lessons paper; PGS002054: LDpred2 from a UKB portability paper) and a cost-effectiveness/screening-oriented paper score (PGS003429), which domain guidance treats as weaker evidence of being the best standalone PRS. However, the decision remains sub-optimal because the most informative PRS-comparable performance evidence is limited/heterogeneous across candidates: PGS003972 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.69) without PRS-only AUROC/R2, while PGS001784 reports a small covariates-regressed-out R2 (~0.0147) but is clearly a framework score; additionally, PGS003973 reports a high C-index (0.882) but with unclear comparability (time-to-event vs case-control not stated) and could be heavily covariate-driven even if only basic covariates are listed. With these comparability limitations and missing incremental/PGS-only AUCs for most candidates, confidence is moderate rather than high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/efo and have phenotype labels consistent with abdominal aortic aneurysm (PGS000753 is explicitly prevalent AAA; the others are generic AAA). Two candidates (PGS003972/PGS003973) come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; many contributing cohorts listed), which domain guidance suggests should generally be preferred over pan-trait/framework scores when endpoints are comparable. Among these, PGS003972 has a full-model AUROC of 0.69 (European eval; n=6,940) while PGS003973 reports a higher full-model C-index of 0.882 (European eval; n=7,517) but with a different covariate set and metric type; neither provides PRS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental performance, so the very high 0.882 is not directly comparable and could be covariate-driven per the provided policy. Other competitors are framework/portability-style (PGS001784 ‘Global Biobank analyses…’ and PGS002054 ‘Portability of 245 polygenic scores…’) or older sparse P+T (PGS000753), and their reported metrics (e.g., R2≈0.014–0.015 or partial-r=0.0144) do not clearly dominate the disease-focused meta-analysis package. Selection remains low-confidence because key comparable PRS-only metrics are missing for most models, covariates are unknown for PGS003972, and PGS003972 vs PGS003973 is not cleanly resolvable from the visible evidence without risking over-weighting a non-comparable full-model discrimination statistic."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/EFO and have broadly aligned endpoints (AAA diagnosis; one is explicitly prevalent). Two candidates (PGS001784, PGS002054) come from pan-trait/framework/portability papers, which domain guidance says should generally not outrank disease-focused scores unless they have clearly superior endpoint and PRS-comparable metrics; their reported metrics are limited (PGS001784 reports a small covariates-regressed-out R2=0.014661 with full-model AUROC=0.868 that may be largely covariate-driven; PGS002054 reports partial-r=0.0144 without AUROC/R2). PGS003429 is from a screening/cost-effectiveness paper and only reports full-model AUROC (0.708) with unknown covariates, making PRS contribution hard to compare. The Nat Genet AAA meta-analysis scores (PGS003972/PGS003973) are disease-focused and multi-cohort, but only full-model AUROC/C-index are shown and covariates are unknown/minimal; the very high C-index (0.882) is not interpretable as PRS-only and cannot be cleanly compared here. PGS000753 (MVP AAA study) is disease-focused, uses basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and provides a clear PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, European validation), making it the best-supported choice from the visible evidence despite sparse PRS-comparable AUC/R2 reporting across the set. Overall confidence is limited because most candidates lack directly comparable PRS-only discrimination metrics, so the choice relies on study archetype + covariate cleanliness + effect-size evidence rather than head-to-head PRS-only performance."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/efo and have phenotype alignment to abdominal aortic aneurysm (PGS000753 is prevalent AAA; the others report AAA broadly). Two candidates (PGS003972/PGS003973) come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023) with large multi-cohort development, which domain guidance prefers over pan-trait/portability frameworks when endpoint fidelity is comparable; in contrast, PGS001784 (Cell Genom 2022) and PGS002054 (Am J Hum Genet 2022) are explicitly framework-style (global biobank / UKB portability), and PGS003429 is a screening/cost-effectiveness context with unknown covariates and only full-model AUROC. Between the Nat Genet pair, the visible metadata are insufficient to make a high-confidence choice: PGS003973 reports a high full-model C-index (0.882) but uses only age/age^2/sex covariates and lacks any PRS-only metric, making it unclear how much is PRS-driven; PGS003972 reports a lower full-model AUROC (0.69) and also lacks PRS-only metrics. Given the domain rule to avoid over-weighting full-model discrimination when PRS-only metrics are absent, I select PGS003972 as the preferred disease-focused direct-match PRS, but confidence remains low due to the lack of comparable PRS-only performance metrics and the unresolved ambiguity between PGS003972 and PGS003973."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping (mostly generic AAA; PGS000753 is explicitly prevalent AAA). Two candidates (PGS001784, PGS002054) come from pan-trait/portability framework papers per publication titles, which domain guidance says to down-rank when disease-focused alternatives exist. PGS003429 is from a screening cost-effectiveness paper and reports only full-model AUROC (0.708) with unknown covariates, making PRS comparability unclear; PGS003972/PGS003973 (Nat Genet AAA meta-analysis) also report only full-model metrics (AUROC 0.69 or C-index 0.882) with limited PRS-only evidence and (for PGS003972) unknown covariates. PGS000753 (Circulation, AAA-focused MVP paper) provides the clearest PRS-specific signal via an odds ratio per SD (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates and multi-ancestry evaluation context, without relying on covariate-inflated full-model discrimination. Limitation: PGS000753 is sparse (29 variants) and lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2, while other candidates have larger validation sets but with less comparable (full-model) metrics; therefore the direct-match choice is supported but not unequivocally strongest across fully comparable performance metrics."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is prevalent AAA). Two candidates (PGS003972, PGS003973) come from a disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis publication (Nat Genet 2023) with broad multi-cohort development, which domain guidance suggests should generally outrank pan-trait/framework or portability sweep scores when endpoints are comparable. Between those, PGS003973 reports a very high full-model C-index (0.882) but with only basic age/age^2/sex covariates and no PRS-only metric; given the heritability sanity-check guidance and lack of incremental/PGS-only reporting, that full-model metric is not strong evidence of PRS contribution and could be largely covariate-driven. PGS003972 has similarly disease-focused provenance and reports a more modest AUROC (0.69), also without PRS-only metrics, but avoids relying on an unusually high full-model discrimination value as the main selection signal. Remaining limitation: key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC, incremental AUROC, or covariates-regressed-out R2) are missing or non-comparable across most candidates (some are framework papers with modest PRS-only R2/partial-r), so the choice is based mainly on study archetype/endpoint fidelity rather than definitive comparable performance—hence sub-optimal outcome and moderate confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/efo and have endpoint-aligned phenotyping_reported (mostly generic AAA; PGS000753 is prevalent AAA but still aligned). Between these two, PGS003972 has a full-model AUROC of 0.69, while PGS003973 reports a higher C-index (0.882) but with only age/age^2/sex covariates and without any PRS-only metric; that high discrimination could be largely covariate-driven and is not directly comparable to PRS-only performance. Other alternatives are more framework-like (PGS001784 from a global biobank lessons paper; PGS002054 from a UKB portability sweep) or older/sparser (PGS000753 P+T 29 variants) and/or report only weak PRS-comparable metrics (partial-r≈0.0144; PGS-only R2≈0.0147).
